page.overview:
What is Corsairs of Umbar?

The Corsairs of Umbar were a race of Men hailing from Umbar, south of Gondor. Known for their naval piracy along Gondor's coasts, they were eventually recruited by the Dark Lord Sauron as privateers.

In the Second Age, the Númenóreans began making permanent settlements in Middle-earth such as Umbar, a haven on the Bay of Belfalas' southern shores, and oppressed the natives. Umbar became a fortress of the King's Men, a proud faction loyal to the King of Númenor and opposed to both the Valar and the Eldar.

After the Downfall of Númenor, the Umbar settlers were those whom the Dúnedain called Black Númenóreans, renegades that worshipped Sauron. Even after their master's defeat in the War of the Last Alliance, they continued hostilities with the Gondorians until the year 933 of the Third Age, when Umbar was conquered by Gondor. However for over a hundred years Umbar was besieged by the Black Númenóreans and their Haradrim allies until TA 1050, when they were heavily defeated by King Hyarmendacil I of Gondor.

During the Kin-strife, the defeated rebels of Gondor fled to Umbar, and came to be called Corsairs, most of them being southern Dúnedain, led by the descendants of Castamir the Usurper. For the next 362 years the Corsairs were a menace to Gondor, ravaging its coasts. With knowledge provided by their spies, Angamaitë and Sangahyando commanded an attack in TA 1634 against Pelargir, sacking the city and killing King Minardil. In TA 1810 Gondor retook Umbar, ending the line of Castamir. However Gondor's possession was not to last long and soon Umbar was lost to the Haradrim and new Corsairs, mostly of Haradrim descent, emerged. In TA 2758, they were goaded by the emissaries of Sauron into allying with the Haradrim, Easterlings and Dunlendings against the Gondorians and Rohirrim. Five fleets from Umbar and Harad engaged Gondor, allowing the Wildmen and the "Eastern invaders" to launch their assault upon Rohan. They were repelled with great difficulty by the end of the Long Winter and their allies perished or retreated.
